title: Plane (mathematics)
body:
In mathematics, a plane is a two-dimensional space or flat surface that extends indefinitely. 
A plane is the two-dimensional analogue of a point, a line and three-dimensional space. When working exclusively in two-dimensional Euclidean space, the definite article is used, so the Euclidean plane refers to the whole space.

quiz.q:
Which topic is this? “____ is a two-dimensional space or flat surface that extends indefinitely. 
A ____ is the two-dimensional analogue of a point, a line and three-dimensional space.”
quiz.explanation: That was Plane (mathematics), from your Star Chart.

title: Coplanarity
body: In geometry, a set of points in space are coplanar if there exists a geometric plane that contains them all. For example, three points are always coplanar, and if the points are distinct and non-collinear, the plane they determine is unique. However, a set of four or more distinct points will, in general, not lie in a single plane.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ are coplanar if there exists a geometric plane that contains them all. For example, three points are always coplanar, and if the points are distinct and non-collinear, the plane they determine is unique.”
quiz.explanation: That was Coplanarity, from your Star Chart.

title: Angle
body: In geometry, an angle is formed by two lines that meet at a point. Each line is called a side of the angle, and the point they share is called the vertex of the angle. The term angle is used to denote both geometric figures and their size or magnitude as associated quantity. Angular measure or measure of angle are sometimes used to distinguish between the measure of the figure, as a real number, and the geometric figure itself. The measurement of angles is intrinsically linked with circles and rotations, and this is often visualized or defined using the arc of a circle centered at the vertex and lying between the sides.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is formed by two lines that meet at a point. Each line is called a side of the ____, and the point they share is called the vertex of the ____.”
quiz.explanation: That was Angle, from your Star Chart.

title: Right angle
body: In geometry and trigonometry, a right angle is an angle of exactly 90 degrees or ⁠/2⁠ radians corresponding to a quarter turn. If a ray is placed so that its endpoint is on a line and the adjacent angles are equal, then they are right angles. The term is a calque of Latin angulus rectus; here rectus means "upright", referring to the vertical perpendicular to a horizontal base line.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is an ____ of exactly 90 degrees or ⁠/2⁠ radians corresponding to a quarter turn. If a ray is placed so that its endpoint is on a line and the adjacent angles are equal, then they are ____ angles.”
quiz.explanation: That was Right angle, from your Star Chart.

title: Dihedral angle
body: A dihedral angle is the angle between two intersecting planes or half-planes. It is a plane angle formed on a third plane, perpendicular to the line of intersection between the two planes or the common edge between the two half-planes. In higher dimensions, a dihedral angle represents the angle between two hyperplanes. In chemistry, it is the clockwise angle between half-planes through two sets of three atoms, having two atoms in common.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is the ____ between two intersecting planes or half-planes. It is a plane ____ formed on a third plane, perpendicular to the line of intersection between the two planes or the common edge between the two half-planes.”
quiz.explanation: That was Dihedral angle, from your Star Chart.

title: Internal and external angles
body: In geometry, an angle of a polygon is formed by two adjacent sides. For a simple polygon (non-self-intersecting), regardless of whether it is convex or non-convex, this angle is called an internal angle if a point within the angle is in the interior of the polygon. A polygon has exactly one internal angle per vertex.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is formed by two adjacent sides.”
quiz.explanation: That was Internal and external angles, from your Star Chart.

title: Conic section
body: A conic section, conic or a quadratic curve is a curve obtained from a cone's surface intersecting a plane. The three types of conic section are the hyperbola, the parabola, and the ellipse; the circle is a special case of the ellipse, though it was sometimes considered a fourth type. The ancient Greek mathematicians studied conic sections, culminating around 200 BC with Apollonius of Perga's systematic work on their properties.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a curve obtained from a cone's surface intersecting a plane.”
quiz.explanation: That was Conic section, from your Star Chart.

title: Circle
body: A circle is a shape consisting of all points in a plane that are at a given distance from a given point, the centre. The distance between any point of the circle and the centre is called the radius. The length of a line segment connecting two points on the circle and passing through the centre is called the diameter. A circle bounds a region of the plane called a disc.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a shape consisting of all points in a plane that are at a given distance from a given point, the centre. The distance between any point of the ____ and the centre is called the radius.”
quiz.explanation: That was Circle, from your Star Chart.

title: Circumference
body:
In geometry, the circumference is the perimeter of a circle or ellipse. The circumference is the arc length of the circle, as if it were opened up and straightened out to a line segment. More generally, the perimeter is the curve length around any closed figure. 
Circumference may also refer to the circle itself, that is, the locus corresponding to the edge of a disk. 
The circumference of a sphere is the circumference, or length, of any one of its great circles.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is the perimeter of a circle or ellipse. The ____ is the arc length of the circle, as if it were opened up and straightened out to a line segment.”
quiz.explanation: That was Circumference, from your Star Chart.

title: Radius
body: In classical geometry, a radius of a circle or sphere is any of the line segments from its center to its perimeter (circle) or surface (sphere), and, in more modern usage, it is also their length. The radius of a regular polygon is the line segment or distance from its center to any of its vertices. The name comes from the Latin radius, meaning ray but also the spoke of a chariot wheel. The typical abbreviation and mathematical symbol for radius is R or r. By extension, the diameter is defined as twice the radius:

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is any of the line segments from its center to its perimeter (circle) or surface (sphere), and, in more modern usage, it is also their length.”
quiz.explanation: That was Radius, from your Star Chart.

title: Ellipse
body: In mathematics, an ellipse is a plane curve surrounding two focal points, such that for all points on the curve, the sum of both distances to the two focal points is a constant. It generalizes a circle, which is the special type of ellipse in which the two focal points are the same. The elongation of an ellipse is measured by its eccentricity , a number ranging from  to .

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a plane curve surrounding two focal points, such that for all points on the curve, the sum of both distances to the two focal points is a constant.”
quiz.explanation: That was Ellipse, from your Star Chart.

title: Parabola
body: In mathematics, a parabola is a plane curve which is mirror-symmetrical and is approximately U-shaped. It fits several superficially different mathematical descriptions, which can all be proved to define exactly the same curves.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a plane curve which is mirror-symmetrical and is approximately U-shaped. It fits several superficially different mathematical descriptions, which can all be proved to define exactly the same curves.”
quiz.explanation: That was Parabola, from your Star Chart.

title: Hyperbola
body: In mathematics, a hyperbola is a type of smooth curve lying in a plane, defined by its geometric properties or by equations for which it is the solution set. A hyperbola has two pieces, called connected components or branches, that are mirror images of each other and resemble two infinite bows. The hyperbola is one of the three kinds of conic section, formed by the intersection of a plane and a double cone. If the plane intersects both halves of the double cone but does not pass through the apex of the cones, then the conic is a hyperbola.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a type of smooth curve lying in a plane, defined by its geometric properties or by equations for which it is the solution set.”
quiz.explanation: That was Hyperbola, from your Star Chart.

title: Cardioid
body: In geometry, a cardioid is a plane curve traced by a point on the perimeter of a circle that is rolling around a fixed circle of the same radius. It can also be defined as an epicycloid having a single cusp. It is also a type of sinusoidal spiral, and an inverse curve of the parabola with the focus as the center of inversion. It can also be defined as the set of points of reflections of a fixed point on a circle through all tangents to the circle.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a plane curve traced by a point on the perimeter of a circle that is rolling around a fixed circle of the same radius. It can also be defined as an epicycloid having a single cusp.”
quiz.explanation: That was Cardioid, from your Star Chart.

title: Cycloid
body: In geometry, a cycloid is the curve traced by a point on a circle as it rolls along a straight line without slipping. A cycloid is a specific form of trochoid and is an example of a roulette, a curve generated by a curve rolling on another curve.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is the curve traced by a point on a circle as it rolls along a straight line without slipping. A ____ is a specific form of trochoid and is an example of a roulette, a curve generated by a curve rolling on another curve.”
quiz.explanation: That was Cycloid, from your Star Chart.

title: Brachistochrone curve
body: In physics and mathematics, a brachistochrone curve, or curve of fastest descent, is the one lying on the plane between a point A and a lower point B, where B is not directly below A, on which a bead from rest slides frictionlessly under the influence of a uniform gravitational field to a given end point in the shortest time. The problem was posed by Johann Bernoulli in 1696 and famously solved in one night by Isaac Newton in 1697, though Bernoulli and several others had already found solutions of their own months earlier.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is the one lying on the plane between a point A and a lower point B, where B is not directly below A, on which a bead from rest slides frictionlessly under the influence of a uniform gravitational field to a given end point in the shortest time.”
quiz.explanation: That was Brachistochrone curve, from your Star Chart.

title: Lemniscate
body: In algebraic geometry, a lemniscate is any of several figure-eight or ∞-shaped curves. The word comes from the Latin lēmniscātus, meaning "decorated with ribbons", from the Greek λημνίσκος (lēmnískos), meaning "ribbon", or which alternatively may refer to the wool from which ribbons were made.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is any of several figure-eight or ∞-shaped curves.”
quiz.explanation: That was Lemniscate, from your Star Chart.

title: Elliptic curve
body: In mathematics, an elliptic curve is a smooth, projective, algebraic curve of genus one, on which there is a specified point O. An elliptic curve is defined over a field K and describes points in K2, the Cartesian product of K with itself. If the field's characteristic is different from 2 and 3, then the curve can be described as a plane algebraic curve which consists of solutions (x, y) for:

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a smooth, projective, algebraic ____ of genus one, on which there is a specified point O. An ____ is defined over a field K and describes points in K2, the Cartesian product of K with itself.”
quiz.explanation: That was Elliptic curve, from your Star Chart.

title: Catenary
body: In physics and geometry, a catenary is the curve that an idealized hanging chain or cable assumes under its own weight when supported only at its ends in a uniform gravitational field.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is the curve that an idealized hanging chain or cable assumes under its own weight when supported only at its ends in a uniform gravitational field.”
quiz.explanation: That was Catenary, from your Star Chart.

title: Parallel (geometry)
body: In geometry, parallel lines are coplanar infinite straight lines that do not intersect at any point. Parallel planes are infinite flat planes in the same three-dimensional space that never meet. In three-dimensional Euclidean space, a line and a plane that do not share a point are also said to be parallel. However, two noncoplanar lines are called skew lines. Line segments and Euclidean vectors are parallel if they have the same direction or opposite direction.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ are coplanar infinite straight lines that do not intersect at any point. ____ planes are infinite flat planes in the same three-dimensional space that never meet.”
quiz.explanation: That was Parallel (geometry), from your Star Chart.

title: Perpendicular
body: In geometry, two geometric objects are perpendicular if they intersect at right angles, i.e. at an angle of 90 degrees or π/2 radians. The condition of perpendicularity may be represented graphically using the perpendicular symbol, ⟂. Perpendicular intersections can happen between two lines, between a line and a plane, and between two planes.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “e. at an angle of 90 degrees or π/2 radians. The condition of perpendicularity may be represented graphically using the ____ symbol, ⟂. ____ intersections can happen between two lines, between a line and a plane, and between two planes.”
quiz.explanation: That was Perpendicular, from your Star Chart.

title: Tangent
body: In geometry, the tangent line (or simply tangent) to a plane curve at a given point is, intuitively, the straight line that "just touches" the curve at that point. Leibniz defined it as the line through a pair of infinitely close points on the curve. More precisely, a straight line is tangent to the curve y = f(x) at a point x = c if the line passes through the point (c, f(c)) on the curve and has slope f'(c), where f' is the derivative of f. A similar definition applies to space curves and curves in n-dimensional Euclidean space.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is, intuitively, the straight line that "just touches" the curve at that point. Leibniz defined it as the line through a pair of infinitely close points on the curve.”
quiz.explanation: That was Tangent, from your Star Chart.

title: Line–line intersection
body: In Euclidean geometry, the intersection of a line and a line can be the empty set, a single point, or a line. Distinguishing these cases and finding the intersection have uses, for example, in computer graphics, motion planning, and collision detection.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “In Euclidean geometry, the ____ of a line and a line can be the empty set, a single point, or a line. Distinguishing these cases and finding the ____ have uses, for example, in computer graphics, motion planning, and collision detection.”
quiz.explanation: That was Line–line intersection, from your Star Chart.

title: Triangle
body: A triangle or trigon is a polygon consisting of three sides connected at three corners. It is one of the basic shapes in geometry and the simplest of polygons. The corners, also called vertices, are zero-dimensional points while the sides connecting them, also called edges, are one-dimensional line segments. A triangle has three internal angles, each one bounded by a pair of adjacent sides; the sum of angles of a triangle always equals a straight angle. The triangle is a plane figure and its interior is a planar region. Sometimes an arbitrary edge is chosen to be the base, in which case the opposite vertex is called the apex; the shortest segment between the base and apex is the height. The area of a triangle equals one-half the product of height and base length.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a polygon consisting of three sides connected at three corners. It is one of the basic shapes in geometry and the simplest of polygons.”
quiz.explanation: That was Triangle, from your Star Chart.

title: Equilateral triangle
body: An equilateral triangle is a triangle with three sides of equal length and three equal angles. It is a regular polygon, occasionally known as the regular triangle. It is a special case of an isosceles triangle by modern definition. Its internal angle is 60 degrees or π/3 radians. Its perimeter is three times the side length. Its area is a quarter of the square root of three multiplied with its squared side length. Its appearance is unchanged by three reflection lines, each of which passing through a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite edge, and three rotations around its centroid ; this property is related to the dihedral group of order 6 in algebra.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a ____ with three sides of equal length and three equal angles. It is a regular polygon, occasionally known as the regular ____. It is a special case of an isosceles ____ by modern definition.”
quiz.explanation: That was Equilateral triangle, from your Star Chart.

title: Isosceles triangle
body:
In geometry, an isosceles triangle is a triangle that has two sides of equal length and two angles of equal measure. Sometimes it is specified as having exactly two sides of equal length, and sometimes as having at least two sides of equal length, the latter version thus including the equilateral triangle as a special case.
Examples of isosceles triangles include the isosceles right triangle, the golden triangle, and the faces of bipyramids and certain Catalan solids.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a ____ that has two sides of equal length and two angles of equal measure.”
quiz.explanation: That was Isosceles triangle, from your Star Chart.

title: Reuleaux triangle
body: A Reuleaux triangle is a curved triangle with constant width, the simplest and best known curve of constant width other than the circle. It is formed from the intersection of three equally sized circular disks, each centered on the boundary of the other two. Constant width means that the separation of every two parallel supporting lines is the same, independent of their orientation. Because its width is constant, the Reuleaux triangle is one answer to the question "Other than a circle, what shape can a manhole cover be made so that it cannot fall down through the hole?"

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a curved ____ with constant width, the simplest and best known curve of constant width other than the circle. It is formed from the intersection of three equally sized circular disks, each centered on the boundary of the other two.”
quiz.explanation: That was Reuleaux triangle, from your Star Chart.

title: Right triangle
body: A right triangle or right-angled triangle, sometimes called an orthogonal triangle or rectangular triangle, is a triangle in which two sides are perpendicular, forming a right angle.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a ____ in which two sides are perpendicular, forming a ____ angle.”
quiz.explanation: That was Right triangle, from your Star Chart.

title: Quadrilateral
body: In geometry, a quadrilateral is a four-sided polygon, having four edges (sides) and four corners (vertices). The word is derived from the Latin words quadri, a variant of four, and latus, meaning "side". It is also called a tetragon, derived from Greek "tetra" meaning "four" and "gon" meaning "corner" or "angle", in analogy to other polygons. Since "gon" means "angle", it is analogously called a quadrangle, or 4-angle. A quadrilateral with vertices , ,  and  is sometimes denoted as .

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a four-sided polygon, having four edges (sides) and four corners (vertices). The word is derived from the Latin words quadri, a variant of four, and latus, meaning "side".”
quiz.explanation: That was Quadrilateral, from your Star Chart.

title: Square
body: In geometry, a square is a regular quadrilateral. It has four straight sides of equal length and four equal angles. Squares are special cases of rectangles, which have four equal angles, and of rhombuses, which have four equal sides. As with all rectangles, a square's angles are right angles, making adjacent sides perpendicular. The area of a square is the side length multiplied by itself, and so in algebra, multiplying a number by itself is called squaring.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a regular quadrilateral. It has four straight sides of equal length and four equal angles. Squares are special cases of rectangles, which have four equal angles, and of rhombuses, which have four equal sides.”
quiz.explanation: That was Square, from your Star Chart.

title: Rectangle
body: In Euclidean plane geometry, a rectangle is a rectilinear convex polygon or a quadrilateral with four right angles. It can also be defined as: an equiangular quadrilateral, since equiangular means that all of its angles are equal ; or a parallelogram containing a right angle. A rectangle with four sides of equal length is a square. The term "oblong" is used to refer to a non-square rectangle. A rectangle with vertices ABCD would be denoted as  ABCD.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a rectilinear convex polygon or a quadrilateral with four right angles.”
quiz.explanation: That was Rectangle, from your Star Chart.

title: Parallelogram
body: In Euclidean geometry, a parallelogram is a chiral simple (non-self-intersecting) quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides. The opposite or facing sides of a parallelogram are of equal length and the opposite angles of a parallelogram are of equal measure. The congruence of opposite sides and opposite angles is a direct consequence of the Euclidean parallel postulate and neither condition can be proven without appealing to the Euclidean parallel postulate or one of its equivalent formulations.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a chiral simple (non-self-intersecting) quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides.”
quiz.explanation: That was Parallelogram, from your Star Chart.

title: Rhombus
body: In geometry, a rhombus is an equilateral quadrilateral, a quadrilateral whose four sides all have the same length. Other names for rhombus include diamond, lozenge, and calisson.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is an equilateral quadrilateral, a quadrilateral whose four sides all have the same length. Other names for ____ include diamond, lozenge, and calisson.”
quiz.explanation: That was Rhombus, from your Star Chart.

title: Regular polygon
body: In Euclidean geometry, a regular polygon is a polygon that is direct equiangular and equilateral. Regular polygons may be either convex or star. In the limit, a sequence of regular polygons with an increasing number of sides approximates a circle, if the perimeter or area is fixed, or a regular apeirogon, if the edge length is fixed.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a ____ that is direct equiangular and equilateral. ____ polygons may be either convex or star.”
quiz.explanation: That was Regular polygon, from your Star Chart.

title: Star polygon
body: In geometry, a star polygon is a type of non-convex polygon. Regular star polygons have been studied in depth; while star polygons in general appear not to have been formally defined, certain notable ones can arise through truncation operations on regular simple or star polygons.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a type of non-convex ____.”
quiz.explanation: That was Star polygon, from your Star Chart.

title: Pentagram
body: A pentagram is a regular five-pointed star polygon, formed from the diagonal line segments of a convex regular pentagon. Drawing a circle around the five points creates a similar symbol referred to as the pentacle, which is used widely by Wiccans and in paganism, or as a sign of life and connections, but there is also an inverted version.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a regular five-pointed star polygon, formed from the diagonal line segments of a convex regular pentagon.”
quiz.explanation: That was Pentagram, from your Star Chart.

title: Three-dimensional space
body: In geometry, a three-dimensional space is a mathematical space in which three values are required to determine the position of a point. Alternatively, it can be referred to as 3-space. Most commonly, it means the three-dimensional Euclidean space, which is the Euclidean space of dimension three, which models physical space. More general three-dimensional spaces are called 3-manifolds.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a mathematical ____ in which three values are required to determine the position of a point. Alternatively, it can be referred to as 3-____.”
quiz.explanation: That was Three-dimensional space, from your Star Chart.

title: Solid geometry
body:
Solid geometry or stereometry is the geometry of three-dimensional Euclidean space .
A solid figure is the region of 3D space bounded by a two-dimensional closed surface; for example, a solid ball consists of a sphere and its interior.

quiz.q:
Which topic is this? “____ is the ____ of three-dimensional Euclidean space .
A ____ figure is the region of 3D space bounded by a two-dimensional closed surface; for example, a ____ ball consists of a sphere and its interior.”
quiz.explanation: That was Solid geometry, from your Star Chart.

title: Surface (mathematics)
body: In mathematics, a surface is a mathematical model of the common concept of a surface. It is a generalization of a plane, but, unlike a plane, it may be curved. An example of a non-flat surface is the sphere.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a mathematical model of the common concept of a ____. It is a generalization of a plane, but, unlike a plane, it may be curved. An example of a non-flat ____ is the sphere.”
quiz.explanation: That was Surface (mathematics), from your Star Chart.

title: Surface of revolution
body:
A surface of revolution is a surface in Euclidean space created by rotating a curve one full revolution around an axis of rotation .
The volume bounded by the surface created by this revolution is the solid of revolution.

quiz.q:
Which topic is this? “____ is a ____ in Euclidean space created by rotating a curve one full ____ around an axis of rotation .
The volume bounded by the ____ created by this ____ is the solid of ____.”
quiz.explanation: That was Surface of revolution, from your Star Chart.

title: Torus
body: In geometry, a torus is a surface of revolution generated by revolving a circle in three-dimensional space one full revolution about an axis that is coplanar with the circle. The main types of tori include ring tori, horn tori, and spindle tori. A ring torus is sometimes colloquially referred to as a doughnut.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a surface of revolution generated by revolving a circle in three-dimensional space one full revolution about an axis that is coplanar with the circle. The main types of tori include ring tori, horn tori, and spindle tori.”
quiz.explanation: That was Torus, from your Star Chart.

title: Cylinder
body: A cylinder has traditionally been a three-dimensional solid, one of the most basic of curvilinear geometric shapes. In elementary geometry, it is considered a prism with a circle as its base.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “A ____ has traditionally been a three-dimensional solid, one of the most basic of curvilinear geometric shapes. In elementary geometry, it is considered a prism with a circle as its base.”
quiz.explanation: That was Cylinder, from your Star Chart.

title: Möbius strip
body: In mathematics, a Möbius strip, Möbius band, or Möbius loop is a surface that can be formed by attaching the ends of a strip of paper together with a half-twist. As a mathematical object, it was discovered by Johann Benedict Listing and August Ferdinand Möbius in 1858, but it had already appeared in Roman mosaics from the third century CE. The Möbius strip is a non-orientable surface, meaning that within it one cannot consistently distinguish clockwise from counterclockwise turns. Every non-orientable surface contains a Möbius strip.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a surface that can be formed by attaching the ends of a ____ of paper together with a half-twist.”
quiz.explanation: That was Möbius strip, from your Star Chart.

title: Sphere
body: A sphere is a surface analogous to the circle, a curve. In solid geometry, a sphere is the set of points that are all at the same distance r from a given point in three-dimensional space. That given point is the center of the sphere, and the distance r is the sphere's radius. The earliest known mentions of spheres appear in the work of the ancient Greek mathematicians.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a surface analogous to the circle, a curve. In solid geometry, a ____ is the set of points that are all at the same distance r from a given point in three-dimensional space.”
quiz.explanation: That was Sphere, from your Star Chart.

title: Solid angle
body:
In geometry, a solid angle is a measure of the amount of the field of view from some particular point that a given object covers. That is, it is a measure of how large the object appears to an observer looking from that point.
The point from which the object is viewed is called the apex of the solid angle, and the object is said to subtend its solid angle at that point.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a measure of the amount of the field of view from some particular point that a given object covers. That is, it is a measure of how large the object appears to an observer looking from that point.”
quiz.explanation: That was Solid angle, from your Star Chart.

title: Skew lines
body: In three-dimensional geometry, skew lines are two lines that do not intersect and are not parallel. A simple example of a pair of skew lines is the pair of lines through opposite edges of a regular tetrahedron. Two lines that both lie in the same plane must either cross each other or be parallel, so skew lines can exist only in three or more dimensions. Two lines are skew if and only if they are not coplanar.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ are two ____ that do not intersect and are not parallel. A simple example of a pair of ____ is the pair of ____ through opposite edges of a regular tetrahedron.”
quiz.explanation: That was Skew lines, from your Star Chart.

title: Polyhedron
body: In geometry, a polyhedron is a three-dimensional figure with flat polygonal faces, straight edges and sharp corners or vertices. The term "polyhedron" may refer either to a solid figure or to its boundary surface. The terms solid polyhedron and polyhedral surface are commonly used to distinguish the two concepts. Also, the term polyhedron is often used to refer implicitly to the whole structure formed by a solid polyhedron, its polyhedral surface, its faces, its edges, and its vertices.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a three-dimensional figure with flat polygonal faces, straight edges and sharp corners or vertices. The term "____" may refer either to a solid figure or to its boundary surface.”
quiz.explanation: That was Polyhedron, from your Star Chart.

title: Regular polyhedron
body: A regular polyhedron is a polyhedron with regular and congruent polygons as faces. Its symmetry group acts transitively on its flags. A regular polyhedron is highly symmetrical, being all of edge-transitive, vertex-transitive and face-transitive. In classical contexts, many different equivalent definitions are used; a common one is that the faces are congruent regular polygons which are assembled in the same way around each vertex.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a ____ with ____ and congruent polygons as faces. Its symmetry group acts transitively on its flags. A ____ is highly symmetrical, being all of edge-transitive, vertex-transitive and face-transitive.”
quiz.explanation: That was Regular polyhedron, from your Star Chart.

title: Platonic solid
body: In geometry, a Platonic solid is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space. Being a regular polyhedron means that the faces are congruent regular polygons, and the same number of faces meet at each vertex. There are only five such polyhedra: the regular tetrahedron, the cube, the regular octahedron, the regular dodecahedron, and the regular icosahedron.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space. Being a regular polyhedron means that the faces are congruent regular polygons, and the same number of faces meet at each vertex.”
quiz.explanation: That was Platonic solid, from your Star Chart.

title: Cube
body: A cube is a three-dimensional solid object in geometry. It has eight vertices and twelve straight edges of the same length, so that these edges form six square faces of the same size. It is an example of a polyhedron. It is a special case of a cuboid, a parallelepiped, and a rhombohedron in which all six quadrilateral faces are squares. It is a three-dimensional hypercube, a family of polytopes that also includes the two-dimensional square and four-dimensional tesseract.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a three-dimensional solid object in geometry. It has eight vertices and twelve straight edges of the same length, so that these edges form six square faces of the same size. It is an example of a polyhedron.”
quiz.explanation: That was Cube, from your Star Chart.

title: Pyramid (geometry)
body: A pyramid is a polyhedron formed by connecting a polygonal base and a point, called the apex. Each base edge and apex form a triangle, called a lateral face. A pyramid is a conic solid with a polygonal base.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a polyhedron formed by connecting a polygonal base and a point, called the apex. Each base edge and apex form a triangle, called a lateral face. A ____ is a conic solid with a polygonal base.”
quiz.explanation: That was Pyramid (geometry), from your Star Chart.

title: Tetrahedron
body: In geometry, a tetrahedron, also known as a  triangular pyramid, is a polyhedron composed of four triangular faces, six straight edges, and four vertices. The tetrahedron is the simplest of all the ordinary convex polyhedra.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a polyhedron composed of four triangular faces, six straight edges, and four vertices. The ____ is the simplest of all the ordinary convex polyhedra.”
quiz.explanation: That was Tetrahedron, from your Star Chart.

title: Octahedron
body: In geometry, an octahedron is any polyhedron with eight faces. One special case is the regular octahedron, a Platonic solid composed of eight equilateral triangles, four of which meet at each vertex. Many types of irregular octahedra also exist, including both convex and non-convex shapes.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is any polyhedron with eight faces. One special case is the regular ____, a Platonic solid composed of eight equilateral triangles, four of which meet at each vertex.”
quiz.explanation: That was Octahedron, from your Star Chart.

title: Dodecahedron
body: In geometry, a dodecahedron or duodecahedron is any polyhedron with twelve flat faces. The most familiar dodecahedron is the regular dodecahedron with regular pentagons as faces, which is a Platonic solid. There are also three regular star dodecahedra, which are constructed as stellations of the convex form. All of these have icosahedral symmetry, order 120.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is any polyhedron with twelve flat faces. The most familiar ____ is the regular ____ with regular pentagons as faces, which is a Platonic solid.”
quiz.explanation: That was Dodecahedron, from your Star Chart.

title: Regular dodecahedron
body: A regular dodecahedron or pentagonal dodecahedron is a dodecahedron composed of regular pentagonal faces, three meeting at each vertex. It is one of the Platonic solids, described in Plato's dialogues as the shape of the universe itself. Johannes Kepler used the dodecahedron in his 1596 model of the Solar System. However, the dodecahedron and other Platonic solids had already been described by other philosophers since antiquity.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a ____ composed of ____ pentagonal faces, three meeting at each vertex. It is one of the Platonic solids, described in Plato's dialogues as the shape of the universe itself.”
quiz.explanation: That was Regular dodecahedron, from your Star Chart.

title: Icosahedron
body: In geometry, an icosahedron is a polyhedron with 20 faces. The name comes from Ancient Greek  εἴκοσι (eíkosi) 'twenty' and  ἕδρα (hédra) 'seat'. The plural can be either "icosahedra" or "icosahedrons".

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a polyhedron with 20 faces. The name comes from Ancient Greek  εἴκοσι (eíkosi) 'twenty' and  ἕδρα (hédra) 'seat'. The plural can be either "icosahedra" or "icosahedrons".”
quiz.explanation: That was Icosahedron, from your Star Chart.

title: Regular icosahedron
body: The regular icosahedron is a convex polyhedron that can be constructed from a pentagonal antiprism by attaching two pentagonal pyramids with regular faces to each of its pentagonal faces, or by putting points onto the cube. The resulting polyhedron has 20 equilateral triangles as its faces, 30 edges, and 12 vertices. It is an example of a Platonic solid and of a deltahedron. The icosahedral graph represents the skeleton of a regular icosahedron.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a convex polyhedron that can be constructed from a pentagonal antiprism by attaching two pentagonal pyramids with ____ faces to each of its pentagonal faces, or by putting points onto the cube.”
quiz.explanation: That was Regular icosahedron, from your Star Chart.

title: Prism (geometry)
body: In geometry, a prism is a polyhedron comprising an n-sided polygon base, a second base which is a translated copy of the first, and n other faces, necessarily all parallelograms, joining corresponding sides of the two bases. All cross-sections parallel to the bases are translations of the bases. Prisms are named after their bases, e.g. a prism with a pentagonal base is called a pentagonal prism. Prisms are a subclass of prismatoids.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a polyhedron comprising an n-sided polygon base, a second base which is a translated copy of the first, and n other faces, necessarily all parallelograms, joining corresponding sides of the two bases.”
quiz.explanation: That was Prism (geometry), from your Star Chart.

title: Four-dimensional space
body: Four-dimensional (4D) space is the mathematical extension of the concept of three-dimensional space (3D). Three-dimensional space is the simplest possible abstraction of the observation that one needs only three numbers, called dimensions, to describe the sizes or locations of objects in the everyday world. This concept of ordinary space is called Euclidean space because it corresponds to Euclid's geometry, which was originally abstracted from the spatial experiences of everyday life.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is the mathematical extension of the concept of three-dimensional ____ (3D).”
quiz.explanation: That was Four-dimensional space, from your Star Chart.

title: Rotations in 4-dimensional Euclidean space
body: In mathematics, the group of rotations about a fixed point in four-dimensional Euclidean space is denoted SO(4). The name comes from the fact that it is the special orthogonal group of 4 by 4 real matrices.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is denoted SO(4). The name comes from the fact that it is the special orthogonal group of 4 by 4 real matrices.”
quiz.explanation: That was Rotations in 4-dimensional Euclidean space, from your Star Chart.

title: 3-sphere
body: In mathematics, a hypersphere or 3-sphere is a 4-dimensional analogue of a sphere, and is the 3-dimensional n-sphere. In 4-dimensional Euclidean space, it is the set of points equidistant from a fixed central point. The interior of a 3-sphere is a 4-ball.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a 4-dimensional analogue of a sphere, and is the 3-dimensional n-sphere. In 4-dimensional Euclidean space, it is the set of points equidistant from a fixed central point. The interior of a ____ is a 4-ball.”
quiz.explanation: That was 3-sphere, from your Star Chart.

title: 5-cell
body: In geometry, the 5-cell is the convex 4-polytope with Schläfli symbol {3,3,3}. It is a 5-vertex four-dimensional object bounded by five tetrahedral cells. It is also known as a C5, hypertetrahedron, pentachoron, pentatope, pentahedroid, tetrahedral pyramid, or 4-simplex (Coxeter's α4 polytope), the simplest possible convex 4-polytope, and is analogous to the tetrahedron in three dimensions and the triangle in two dimensions. The 5-cell is a 4-dimensional pyramid with a tetrahedral base and four tetrahedral sides.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is the convex 4-polytope with Schläfli symbol {3,3,3}. It is a 5-vertex four-dimensional object bounded by five tetrahedral cells.”
quiz.explanation: That was 5-cell, from your Star Chart.

title: Tesseract
body: In geometry, a tesseract or 4-cube is a four-dimensional hypercube, analogous to a two-dimensional square and a three-dimensional cube. Just as the perimeter of the square consists of four edges and the surface of the cube consists of six square faces, the hypersurface of the tesseract consists of eight cubical cells, meeting at right angles. The tesseract is one of the six convex regular 4-polytopes.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a four-dimensional hypercube, analogous to a two-dimensional square and a three-dimensional cube.”
quiz.explanation: That was Tesseract, from your Star Chart.

title: 16-cell
body: In geometry, the 16-cell is the regular convex 4-polytope (four-dimensional analogue of a Platonic solid) with Schläfli symbol {3,3,4}. It is one of the six regular convex 4-polytopes first described by the Swiss mathematician Ludwig Schläfli in the mid-19th century. It is also called C16, hexadecachoron, or hexdecahedroid [sic?].

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is the regular convex 4-polytope (four-dimensional analogue of a Platonic solid) with Schläfli symbol {3,3,4}.”
quiz.explanation: That was 16-cell, from your Star Chart.

title: 24-cell
body: In four-dimensional geometry, the 24-cell is a convex regular 4-polytope, a four-dimensional analogue of a Platonic solid. It is named for the 24 octahedra that form its boundary.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a convex regular 4-polytope, a four-dimensional analogue of a Platonic solid. It is named for the 24 octahedra that form its boundary.”
quiz.explanation: That was 24-cell, from your Star Chart.

title: Trigonometry
body: Trigonometry is a branch of mathematics concerned with relationships between angles and side lengths of triangles. In particular, the trigonometric functions relate the angles of a right triangle with ratios of its side lengths. The field emerged in the Hellenistic world during the 3rd century BC from applications of geometry to astronomical studies. The Greeks focused on the calculation of chords, while mathematicians in India created the earliest-known tables of values for trigonometric ratios such as sine.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a branch of mathematics concerned with relationships between angles and side lengths of triangles. In particular, the trigonometric functions relate the angles of a right triangle with ratios of its side lengths.”
quiz.explanation: That was Trigonometry, from your Star Chart.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “In trigonometry, the ____ relates the lengths of the sides of a triangle to the cosine of one of its angles.”
quiz.explanation: That was Law of cosines, from your Star Chart.

title: Law of sines

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a mathematical equation relating the lengths of the sides of any triangle to the ____ of its angles.”
quiz.explanation: That was Law of sines, from your Star Chart.

title: Unit circle
body: In mathematics, a unit circle is a circle of unit radius—that is, a radius of 1. Frequently, especially in trigonometry, the unit circle is the circle of radius 1 centered at the origin in the Cartesian coordinate system in the Euclidean plane. In topology, it is often denoted as S1 because it is a one-dimensional unit n-sphere.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a ____ of unit radius—that is, a radius of 1. Frequently, especially in trigonometry, the ____ is the ____ of radius 1 centered at the origin in the Cartesian coordinate system in the Euclidean plane.”
quiz.explanation: That was Unit circle, from your Star Chart.

title: Topology
body: Topology is the branch of mathematics concerned with the properties of a geometric object that are preserved under continuous deformations, such as stretching, twisting, crumpling, and bending; that is, without closing holes, opening holes, tearing, gluing, or passing through itself.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is the branch of mathematics concerned with the properties of a geometric object that are preserved under continuous deformations, such as stretching, twisting, crumpling, and bending; that is, without closing holes, opening holes, tearing, gluing, or passing through itself.”
quiz.explanation: That was Topology, from your Star Chart.

title: Brouwer fixed-point theorem
body: Brouwer's fixed-point theorem is a fixed-point theorem in topology, named after L. E. J. Brouwer. It states that for any continuous function  mapping a nonempty compact convex set to itself, there is a point  such that . The simplest forms of Brouwer's theorem are for continuous functions  from a closed interval  in the real numbers to itself or from a closed disk  to itself. A more general form than the latter is for continuous functions from a nonempty convex compact subset  of Euclidean space to itself.

quiz.q: Which topic is this? “____ is a ____ ____ in topology, named after L. E. J. ____. It states that for any continuous function  mapping a nonempty compact convex set to itself, there is a point  such that .”
